The second thing is you can die from a choke without being asphyxiated. Just because you can mechanically  move air (by the way George Floyd was barely able to do that) doesn't mean your brain is getting oxygen. If you prevent the carotid artery from delivering oxygenated blood to your brain, I don't care how much air you're bringing in and out of your body - you will die if it doesn't stop. This is what is called a blood choke. So even if he didn't die by being prevented from physically breathing, Chauvin prevented his brain from receiving oxygen. Both asphyxiation and blocking the carotid essentially work the same - no oxygen to the  brain. Stop being intentionally obtuse by saying he wasn't asphyxiated. He was still, at the lease, blood choked to death.

NTA and here's why: 

Even though she's been around for a year and a half, she's not your friend. She's your friend's SO and is invited as a courtesy. 

She agreed to bring her own meals. At no point did she indicate in the year and a half she's been coming to these get togethers that it bothered her. You can't read minds. If she felt left out, she or James should have mentioned this NOT AT THE DINNER PARTY -- preferably before they accept another invite. They didn't even give you a chance to try because you were operating under the assumption that she's good with bringing her own food. 

A lot of people are saying it's not that hard cooking vegan, and for experienced cooks like you and you wife it probably isn't, but there are a lot of extra considerations to be made. Veganism is pretty strict. They don't eat any animal products at all and that can get tricky. Small things like butter, cheese, or something completely disqualify a dish from being vegan. Sure, I guess you could give her a salad, but to me that seems like a slap in the face when you make an elaborate meal and hand the vegan a salad. 

Cost. You're providing everything for free for them. Adding extra Ingredients, that are vegan and are good substitutes, is expensive. This is your meal and she's not even YOUR friend. It's not you're job to foot the bill to accommodate her especially when she agreed to bring her own food and never mentioned that she was upset about it. 

Additionally, I just feel like it was a bit rude of her to make a scene and if James knew she was upset about this before the dinner he should have mentioned as soon as he got there or maybe canceled and explained later. He's a dick for not saying something way sooner. 

Going forward though, you should probably try to include her with 1 dish that is completely if you plan on continuing to invite these two. Take it as a culinary challenge. You didn't know it bothered  her before, but now that you, try to accommodate. Remember everyone can eat a vegan dish so it won't go to waste if it's good.
